author: Slate
title: My Mother-in-Law Plans to Invade My Home. Unfortunately, She's Not Coming Alone.
text:
I'm taking a stand.
My mother-in-law, “Gertrude,” is coming to our city for my brother-in-law’s wedding. She’s insisting on staying at our place—and she’s bringing a wretched plus-one. She has a vile little pomeranian that she got six months ago.
The dog is high strung and prone to attacking people’s ankles, yet she takes the little shit everywhere. I’m terribly allergic to dogs, but Gertrude claims that I can “handle it for a few days,” since none of the hotels around here will allow a dog that isn’t a service animal. My husband has even asked me to “give it a chance”! I’m considering just going over to my parents’ house.
I cannot stand Gertrude or her little four-legged monster. But that also feels like surrendering, because that entitled woman has no right to put me out of my home. What’s the right call? It’s not too late to try to make your husband understand that it’s unacceptable for his mother to drive you from your own home.
Dog-friendly hotels and Airbnbs exist, and he should try to find one for her, or convince her to leave the dog at home. I agree that you shouldn’t have to take refuge at your parents’ place.
But you are severely allergic to dogsyou hate your mother-in-law’s company, so whatever moral victory you might claim by remaining hardly seems worth it. Try again to get your husband to see reason, and if he still refuses, then do whatever you need to do to survive the wedding visit. My 7-year-old daughter thinks she is 17.
She is obsessed with things like crop tops, short shorts, and makeup … none of which we allow her to wear outside of the house. At home with her family, she can wear whatever she wants or play with makeup, but can’t leave the house with it. To be clear, I have not bought her any of these things. She ties her shirts up or wears old shorts that still fit her waist but are way too short.
